title: WhoseJob? — bolder hand
question: A bolder set. Same moment on every card: the dark streetlight at 2100 Clarendon Blvd, Arlington, routed to Dominion instead of the county.

options.label: Data Field
options.lineage: Data-sublime installations: barcode columns and sine lattices in pure black and white
options.thesis: The app's thinking is shown as a data field that scans each check and snaps to the answer.
options.viewport: Black screen; three bar-field columns (district, road, light) scan in turn; the deciding column inverts to white; the answer is set large below with Report and Call.
options.risk: Strong in a video, cold in a resident's hand: no color for levels, and it reads as an art piece before a civic tool. Strobing must stay gentle and stop under reduced motion.

raised.raise: The send action stands alone, separated by deliberate empty space from everything else.
States are marks: outline at rest, filled when pressed, struck through when unavailable, bracketed on focus.
Every report gets a short reference number that is the same on the map, the report, and the email.

options.label: Transit Line
options.lineage: Metropolitan rail diagrams in enamel: colored lines, 45° bends, interchange circles
options.thesis: Your report rides a transit line from your spot to the office, changing lines where ownership changes.
materials: four line inks, one per level of government
options.viewport: Origin station is your pin; the route runs down through District and Road stations on the county's red line, then an interchange: 'Change here — the light is Dominion's', and the amber line ends at the terminus, Dominion Energy, with Report and Call.
options.case: Beats the leader on both axes: VA-08 rides Metro every day, and 'route to the right office' becomes a route people already know how to read.
options.risk: Must not borrow Metro's actual branding or typeface; a dark ground needs careful contrast for older readers.

options.label: Full-Screen Story
options.lineage: Vertical full-screen media feeds: one item fills the screen, an action rail on the right, caption low
options.thesis: Each step is one full screen, like a story: your photo fills it and the answer rises from the bottom.
options.viewport: The resident's photo of the dark light fills the screen; bottom: a level chip, 'Dominion Energy fixes this', the one-line why; right rail: Report, Call, Copy, Map, each with a word under it.
options.case: Beats the leader on both axes: everyone knows this layout, and one thing per screen is GOV.UK's lesson in a form residents already use.
options.risk: Can feel like social media rather than civic; needs a real photo every time, so the no-photo path must still look designed.

options.label: Dark Console
options.viewport: Panels for checks, answer and actions.
options.case: Loses both axes: a developer tool's costume, foreign to residents.
options.kept: The irreversible action stands alone with deliberate space around it.

options.label: Centre-Rail Edition
options.thesis: Two text columns around a keyed rail.
options.viewport: Twin columns with a rail of keys.
options.case: Loses both axes: bookish, and two columns don't fit a phone.
options.kept: States as printed marks: outline, filled, struck, bracketed.

options.label: Catalog Sleeve
options.thesis: Everything numbered, names coded as color strips.
options.viewport: A fac number and a pulse plot.
options.case: Loses both axes: replacing words with color codes fails residents who need plain labels.
options.kept: Every report carries one reference number used everywhere.

canonCard.label: The civic service standard
canonCard.thesis: U.S. Web Design System and GOV.UK patterns, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: White page, blue header, one card with the office, its reason and a blue button.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every government form; nothing for a judge to remember.
